chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim al-Hadrami, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about clay, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Eating clay is forbidden, like the dead animal, blood, and flesh of the pig, except for the clay of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for indeed in it is healing from every illness and security from every fear.'

key_terms.الطِّين: Clay or earth, specifically referring to the substance discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَيْتَة: The dead animal (carrion), a primary example of prohibited food
key_terms.حَرَام: Forbidden or prohibited in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.طِينُ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْن: The clay from the grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating clay in Shia Islam and what is special about the clay of Imam Husayn's grave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a general prohibition on eating clay (ṭīn), equating it with major impurities like dead meat and blood, while carving out a unique exception for the clay of Imam al-Ḥusayn’s (peace be upon him) grave. In Shia tradition, this specific clay (ṭīn al--shamʿ) is revered not merely as a physical substance but as a spiritual medium (wasīla) for healing (shifāʾ) and protection (amān), reflecting the belief in the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt. The ruling underscores the distinction between general culinary prohibitions and the sacred status of relics associated with the Imams.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of our companions, form Ja’far Bin Ibrahim Al Hazramy, from Sa’ad who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the clay. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eating the clay is Prohibited, like the dead, and the blood, and the flesh of the swine, except for the clay of the grave of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, for in it is a healing from every illness, and a security from every fear’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from certain persons of our people from Ja‘far ibn Ibrahim al-Hadramiy from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about clay. He (the Imam) said, ‘ It is unlawful like dead animals, blood, flesh of pigs except the clay from the grave of al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in which there is cure for all kinds of illness and security from all kinds of fear.”’
